title: Run a meeting that decides, include everyone, track your growth

say: Run a meeting that decides, include everyone, and track your growth.
This is the video for Module 2 of Leadership, Identity, and Community Development.

Poorly run meetings drag on and end without a decision. Good ones are short, fair and end with clear actions. Start by writing the purpose in one sentence, such as, agree how members will pay for the new canopy.

say: And choose a time women can attend, such as after market hours, in a safe, accessible venue.

panel.heading: Prepare so the meeting is short and fair
items: Check quorum in your group's rules
A time and place women can attend

say: Follow the same order every time. Open with the customary greeting or prayer, and confirm quorum.
Read the last minutes and adopt them, then check actions from last time.
Take each item in turn. The chair introduces it, invites views and summarises. If someone dominates, say, let us hear from those who have not spoken yet.
Then decide. Use consensus for small groups, a majority vote for clear choices, or delegate detailed tasks to a committee with limits.
Assign actions with names and deadlines, and fix the next date. Share short minutes within 48 hours.

panel.heading: The order of a meeting
panel.rule: Record each decision: who does what, by when.

say: Here is a fair decision in action. The rules say quorum is half the members. 26 of the 40 attend, which is more than 20, so decisions count.
The canopy quote is about 360,000 naira. Get your own quotes, as prices change.
Option A is a one-off levy. 360,000 divided by 40 is 9,000 naira per member.
Option B is the same 9,000 naira, paid as 3,000 naira a month for 3 months.
17 vote for B, 6 for A and 3 abstain. 17 is more than half of the 23 votes cast, so B wins.
The minutes say the treasurer collects monthly, issues receipts and reports the balance at every meeting.

card.title: Paying for the market canopy
rows: Option B: per month, for 3 months

say: A decision made by a few for many often fails. Women with disabilities, widows, young women, women who cannot read and traders working at meeting time are often left out.
So check the time, the venue and the language. Go round the room so quieter members speak first. And read decisions aloud, never only in writing.
Leaders carry a duty of care. Safeguarding means protecting people, especially children, during your activities. Ask permission before posting anyone's photo, and a parent's permission for children.

panel.heading: Keep people, money and data safe

cards.d: Never leave a child alone with one adult behind a closed door. Ask before posting anyone's photo.
A group account with at least two signatories, receipts for every payment, balances at every meeting.
Never share members' numbers, addresses or ID details outside the group without consent.

say: Keep group money in an account with at least two signatories, and issue receipts. Beware of scams that ask leaders to pay a fee to receive a grant. Genuine funders do not charge to release money.

say: Keep a five-minute weekly log: the situation, the skill, what you did, the result, and what you will try next time. For example, Halima counted how often she spoke up. It went from 1 time in week 1 to 4 times in week 4.
When you serve the community, track outputs too. These are what you did, and they are easy to count.

panel.heading: Outputs and outcomes
right: Street no longer floods after rain

say: Outcomes are what actually changed, like a street that no longer floods. Track both, and never inflate your numbers. An honest 12 people came is stronger than a doubtful over 100.

panel.heading: Outputs and outcomes
right: Street no longer floods after rain

say: To remember. Share the agenda ahead and assign roles. Confirm quorum. Bring quiet voices in. Protect people, money and data.
And keep a weekly log, so your growth becomes visible.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Share the agenda ahead and assign roles
Bring quiet and excluded voices in
Log weekly; track outputs and outcomes

say: Now plan or observe a real meeting and write one item of minutes. Audit one group for inclusion and money safety. And start your leadership log, with at least three entries in two weeks.
